summary: This bill requires Medicare-participating hospitals and freestanding birth centers to notify parents of a miscarried fetus within 6 hours of their rights to private burial, cremation, or facility disposal, and to arrange burial or cremation under state fetal death rules if parents elect it in writing within 72 hours.

scores.thoughts: The bill imposes new notification and compliance requirements on hospitals and birth centers participating in Medicare but contains no appropriations, funding mechanisms, or direct spending provisions. Any compliance costs would be indirect and minimal at most.
The bill contains no tax provisions, rate changes, credits, or revenue measures of any kind.

The bill amends Medicare conditions of participation to require hospitals and freestanding birth centers to provide specific notices and options regarding fetal remains after miscarriage. This is a narrow regulatory mandate on healthcare facilities but does not address coverage, payment models, public vs. private systems, or access to care.
The bill has no provisions related to firearms, regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
The bill has no provisions related to immigration, visas, borders, or enforcement.

The bill addresses notification requirements only in cases of miscarriage or stillbirth and makes no reference to abortion procedures, access, restrictions, or fetal rights in the context of elective termination.
The bill has no provisions related to military, defense, or national security spending or policy.
The bill has no provisions related to environmental regulations, climate policy, or natural resources.
The bill has no provisions related to welfare programs, food assistance, or other safety-net benefits.
The bill has no provisions related to schools, education funding, or school choice.
The bill has no provisions related to controlled substances, decriminalization, or enforcement.
The bill creates a private right of civil action for violations but does not address criminal sentencing, policing, or justice system reform.
The bill has no provisions related to trade, tariffs, or globalization.
The bill has no provisions addressing deficits, debt reduction, or fiscal policy.
The bill has no provisions related to LGBTQ+ legal protections or rights.

The bill has no provisions related to technology regulation, data privacy, or digital oversight.
The bill has no provisions related to workers' rights, unions, or employment conditions.
The bill has no provisions addressing religious exemptions, civil rights, or anti-discrimination rules.
